summary: Orphan L0 (15107s old, no active workflow): MCP envelope-markup leak recurrence (DF task 3083): 3 add_memory writes rejected from claude-task-3514-implementer, field=content, matched_pattern=</content>
detail:
OBSERVED: three consecutive mcp__fused-memory__add_memory calls from this session were rejected with error_type=McpEnvelopeMarkupWriteRejected. In each case field='content' and matched_pattern='</content>'. The third rejection returned a storm block (count=3, threshold=3, window_seconds=3600, escalation_id=esc-markup-tripwire-2) stating the upstream serialization leak is ACTIVE.

OBSERVED: the rejections occurred on two different memory payloads (one preferences_and_norms, one observations_and_summaries), and reproduced on a clean retry of the first payload after rewording. Neither payload deliberately quoted MCP markup — no angle-bracket envelope text was authored into either content string.

The tripwire's own hint directs recurrences to DF task 3083 with the agent_id, field and matched_pattern attached; those are recorded above and in the evidence entries. Filing as info, not blocking: the tripwire behaved correctly (it blocked the corrupt writes), the affected content is optional session memory, and task 3514's deliverable is unaffected and fully committed.

Hypothesis: the caller-side tool-call serializer is folding the trailing parameter block of a multi-parameter add_memory invocation into the 'content' value, so the closing '</content>' tag and subsequent parameter tags land inside the payload. NOT verified from this session — I can observe only the rejection response, not the wire payload the server received.</parameter>

resolution:
KNOWN CLASS, ROOT CAUSE ALREADY OWNED — closing close_only (cascades to all 7 members). Re-escalating will not make the fix land sooner. But one member carries a finding the PRD may not cover; I have elevated it rather than let the cascade bury it.

CONFIRMED the containment work is filed and still pending: tasks 3688 (α — shared/src/shared/toolcall_markup.py detector+repairer) and 3689 (β — MarkupGuardMiddleware, the guard that would reject/repair at the FastMCP boundary) are both `pending`, per a live status read this rotation. PRD: plans/toolcall-markup-containment-prd.md, decomposed to 3688-3697 (α-θ). So these recurrences are expected and are NOT a new regression. Six of the seven were caught by the existing markup_tripwire and retried successfully with no data loss — the guard worked as designed.

⚠️ THE ONE THING WORTH CARRYING FORWARD — esc-3664-2 (task 3664, 2026-08-07T01:15Z) is NOT a bare recurrence. It documents an UNGUARDED, PERMANENT corruption on a surface the tripwire does not cover:
- An `mcp__plan-tools__add_design_decision` call wrote a `decision` value and a `rationale` value belonging to TWO DIFFERENT decisions — the rationale stored against "Hand-reapply the reviewer's prose..." is actually the rationale for the separate "keep recon_self_model.py out of scope" decision. A FIELD-CROSSING, not a markup fragment.
- **plan-tools exposes no removal API for design decisions**, so the corrupted entry is PERMANENT in task 3664's plan.json. The reporter compensated by appending a CORRECTION entry and restating both decisions, but the wrong entry remains.
- It happened in the SAME session as a markup leak that the fused-memory tripwire DID catch — i.e. the leak is not confined to fused-memory write paths, which is exactly where the guard sits.
- Both malformed writes were in tool calls with long, multi-field parameter blocks.

SCOPE QUESTION FOR 3689 (β), the actionable item: verify whether MarkupGuardMiddleware is mounted at a boundary that also covers the plan-tools MCP server, or only wraps fused-memory. If only fused-memory, plan-tools writers are an uncovered surface and β's scope should be widened — and 3083's retroactive corpus sweep, if drawn around the memory/task corpus, should include plan.json design-decision entries. Separately, the absence of any removal API means even a detected plan-tools corruption cannot be repaired; consider whether θ or a follow-up needs a removal/replace path.

POSSIBLE LINK TO TASK 3882 — flagged as a HYPOTHESIS, explicitly not asserted. 3882 covers three architects (3079/3243/3065) exiting `subtype='success'` with plan.json entirely MISSING, and 3243's transcript says "the dedup silently dropped my full plan transcription". That is a different shape from field-crossing (total absence vs. mis-assignment), so I am NOT claiming one cause. But both are plan-tools writes going wrong invisibly to the agent, and "dropped in serialization" and "fields crossed in serialization" are the same family. Whoever takes 3882 or 3689 should check whether a shared parameter-serialization failure mode explains both before treating them as unrelated. I have twice this rotation adopted a plausible mechanism without testing it and had to retract, so this stays a lead, not a finding.

CREDIT WHERE DUE, and the reason I trust this member: esc-3664-2's author explicitly wrote "I am NOT asserting a cause" and labelled the shared-serializer idea a hypothesis, noting they did not instrument the harness. That discipline is why its observations are usable as evidence.

Filed as cockpit row df-plantools-markup-coverage-3689.
